why: The migrations are effectively identical — same single-client wrap, same two plugin fixes (orphan function result, first-chunk streaming detector), both verified live and clean on the outside check — so the decision rests on the system-level work, and B's is better evidenced and spans more scales: quality measured where it actually bites (summariser fact-survival across three models, vision hallucination on low-information images), a rework-level proposal to port off the translation bridge that unlocks per-chat cache keys and real usage.cost, per-user spend attribution with the privacy call named, and the finding that N_CHOICES/PRESENCE_PENALTY/MAX_TOKENS<16 silently keep traffic off Router entirely. A is the more decisive package — six built branches, the only serious tier analysis, and the only engineer who actually picked timeout values — but its two biggest cost moves rest on single live samples, and B's own measurements contradict one of them.
A_best: The only engineer to treat tier and model generation as one lever: gpt-5.1 measured live against gpt-4o at both tiers (-44% standard, -71% Flex, ten-times-cheaper cached input, terser answers), with the Flex latency tail correctly split by path — streamed falls back after ~25 s, buffered voice/`/chat` has no such guard — and the model map placed in policy precisely because default_max_tokens/__max_model_tokens/__count_tokens raise NotImplementedError on unknown ids.
B_best: Measuring behaviour, not just price, and letting it kill changes: gpt-4.1-mini was rejected for vision after it described a solid red square as 'a large industrial factory or plant complex' while gpt-4o was correct 4/4, and the cheap summariser stops at 4.1-mini because gpt-4o-mini kept the planted fact only 2 of 3 times — plus the n2 finding that three ordinary config settings route traffic around Router and silently out of every improvement.
A_worst: Recommends gpt-4o-mini for summarisation on one sample ('both summaries carry the same facts') for a call whose output seeds the rest of the conversation — exactly the swap B's 3-sample fact-survival test shows dropping a fact 1 in 3 — and proposes no rework-scale item at all: the Chat-Completions-to-Responses bridge, the legacy functions API and the tiktoken-based budget math are left as permanent fixtures, and no call site is questioned as to whether it needs a model at all.
B_worst: Dismisses the tier lever on a technicality ('gpt-4o has no Flex tier') instead of asking which model would give it one, which is the move A measured at -71%; and leaves the timeout as a decision item with the seconds unpicked, so the SDK's 600 s default stays in production on a user-waiting chat path while several items claim 'loses: nothing' — including fallbacks, whose own rationale admits users will occasionally get another model's voice.
